subject: Post-call: cross-border failover, backups, and retention clarifications
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medsys.io>, Priya Sethi <priya.sethi@medsys.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: cross-border failover, backups, and retention clarifications

Hi Liam / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning — great conversation and helpful context on the regulatory constraints for MedSys. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

High-level takeaways
- Primary requirement: resident data for EU patients must stay within EU regions; no unencrypted cross-border persistence.
- Failover must be demonstrably limited to compatible EU regions for impacted datasets; global read-only caching acceptable only if encrypted and TTL-limited.
- Backup retention: legal team expects ability to set region-scoped retention windows per dataset (e.g., clinical notes = 7 years, telemetry = 1 year).
- Logging/audit: full request/response audit trail required for admin actions; token-level metadata acceptable for generated content.

Open questions from our side (items we promised to follow up on)
1) Cross-region failover behavior: can Redwood guarantee that cold backups and snapshot restores for EU-resident models will never land in non-EU regions? 
2) Backup encryption key management: do you need customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for backups and replicas?
3) RTO/RPO targets acceptable to MedSys for primary model endpoints and for archival restores?
4) Operator access: are there any auditors who need read-only access to logs for compliance audits?

Attachments and links
- I've uploaded a simple architecture diagram that shows how regional routing and snapshot stores would work on Redwood (see attached residency-arch-diagram.pdf).
- Also attaching the SOC2 evidence template you mentioned (SOC2-evidence-request.xlsx) to show where we can map artifacts.

Proposed next steps
- Ben (SE) to outline exact failover mechanics and where snapshots live.
- We send a short technical note that maps the MedSys data classes to our retention controls.
- Schedule a deep-dive with your security/compliance team next week (30–45 min).

Can you confirm which EU regions you prefer we restrict to (e.g., eu-west-1 / eu-central-1) and whether you require CMK for at-rest keys? Once we have that we can produce a succinct SOC-compliance note.

Thanks —

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0127
Redwood Inference

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medsys.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sethi <priya.sethi@medsys.io>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 17:04:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: cross-border failover, backups, and retention clarifications

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick clarifications from our end: 

1) Regions: we must keep EU patient PII within EU only. Primary preference is eu-west-1 (Ireland) and eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) as failover pair. No automatic failover to non-EU under any circumstance.
2) Backups: snapshots and backups must be stored in EU and encrypted with our CMK. We cannot accept vendor-managed keys for backups that contain patient identifiers.
3) Failover behavior: we need a documented runbook that shows what happens during cross-zone vs cross-region failover and an ability to trigger manual failover for a region if automatic behavior would cross jurisdictional boundaries.
4) Logs: security team requires admin/audit logs to be retained 7 years; access to those logs must be auditable via RBAC. Tokenized generation logs may be masked, but full request/response must be exportable for legal review.

Question: for encrypted backups with CMK, does Redwood support customer-managed HSM keys today for both primary storage and snapshot exports? Also, what is the typical RPO we should expect for model KV caches vs full model state restores?

Appreciate you looping in Ben / SE. Priya and I are available most mornings next week for the security deep-dive.

Cheers,
Liam
Head of Cloud Ops | MedSys Health
liam.oconnor@medsys.io

Subject: RE: Post-call: cross-border failover, backups, and retention clarifications

Hi Liam / Priya —

Thanks — answering your questions below and attaching a short technical note.

1) Regions & failover mechanics- Short answer: yes, we can enforce EU-only residency for datasets that are flagged as EU-restricted. Our routing policy supports region-scoped routing rules and explicit region pinning per dataset. Automatic failover stays within the region group (eu-west-1 <-> eu-central-1) when you opt into an EU failover group. Cross-jurisdiction failover to non-EU is treated as a manual escalation and requires an explicit policy override with audit trail.

2) Backups & CMK/HSM- We support customer-managed keys via major KMS providers (AWS KMS with CMK and CloudHSM for HSM-backed keys). Backups and snapshot exports can be configured to use your CMK. We'll include the KMS key policy template in the note.

3) RTO / RPO guidance- For live model endpoints (weights + KV cache): typical RPO is near-zero for KV cache when using continuous replication within the region group; RTO for bringing a standby endpoint online is usually <10 minutes for warmed replicas.
- For cold snapshot restores (full model state + persisted artifacts): RPO depends on snapshot cadence (we support hourly snapshots) and RTO can range from 30–120 minutes depending on model size and restore location. We'll map expected ranges for your largest models in the follow-up doc.

4) Logging and retention- Admin/audit logs: Redwood can retain immutable admin logs for 7+ years in EU object stores. Access is RBAC-protected and we provide exportable chains of custody for audits. Application-level request/response traces can be masked or redacted per dataset; we can provide a compliance-preserving export for legal review.

Attachments
- residency-arch-diagram.pdf (the diagram Hannah shared)
- redwood-msh-eu-residency-note.pdf (technical note)
- ksm-key-policy-template.txt

Action items (owner)
- Ben: send KMS policy template + technical note (today) -> done (attached).
- Hannah: coordinate security deep-dive and include our compliance engineer (Monica) -> propose Wed/Thu morning EU time.
- MedSys: confirm final EU region pair and CMK provider (Priya / Liam).

If helpful I can also sketch a manual failover runbook that shows steps, expected downtime, and required approvals — happy to draft that and iterate with your security team.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
